records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff imports org.keycloak.operator.crds.v2alpha1.deployment.spec.FeatureSpec and calls kc.getSpec().setFeatureSpec(new FeatureSpec()) / getFeatureSpec().getEnabledFeatures(), but the v2alpha1 KeycloakSpec in this branch exposes no featureSpec field — features are configured via spec.getUnsupported()/UnsupportedSpec, so the test file does not compile against the current CRD classes. The operator integration test module fails to compile ('cannot find symbol FeatureSpec' / 'method setFeatureSpec not found'), so the entire operator test suite cannot run and CI blocks the merge.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The Dockerfile unconditionally appends --features=rolling-updates to kc.sh build, but this image script is (via the VERSION arg) also built against previously released Keycloak versions in upgrade tests, and the rolling-updates feature only exists in this new build — an older kc.sh rejects the unknown feature and the build step fails. Any test or workflow that uses Dockerfile-custom-image with VERSION pointing at a pre-rolling-updates release gets 'Unknown feature: rolling-updates' during docker build, breaking the upgrade-path scenarios this script exists to serve.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The feature-disabled branch calls picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) followed by return, relying on AbstractUpdatesCommand exposing an exit(int) exit mechanism whose behavior in this class hierarchy is unverified in the diff; if exit is inherited from a spec/command-line helper that throws, the subsequent statements are unreachable, and if it does not terminate the process the run() method continues to printPreviewWarning() only due to the explicit return — but the metadata command at UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java:46-50 duplicates the same pattern, so any mismatch in exit semantics breaks one but not the other. If picocli.exit does not map the code to the process exit status in this command context (e.g. it only sets an execution result consumed by the runner), scripts checking $? get an unexpected code and mis-classify a feature-disabled failure as a different error class.

Users troubleshooting 'update-compatibility' failures must fix the feature flag before discovering they also have a config error; the two failure modes are reported through the same generic exit path (picocli.exit) with no distinguishing documentation beyond the message, making scripted diagnosis of exit code 4 ambiguous.

records.issue_text: [BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently renumbered from 4 to 3 and the value 4 is repurposed to mean FEATURE_DISABLED, breaking every external caller that checks exit code 4 for 'recreate required'. Any CI job, script, or operator-side wrapper that branches on `exit code == 4` to decide 'rolling upgrade not possible' now silently takes the wrong branch: a genuine recreate-required result returns 3 (which those scripts treat as unknown/error or success-adjacent) and code 4 now signals a completely different condition (feature disabled), so existing automation misclassifies outcomes with no error surfaced at the call site.
records.rationale: The diff explicitly changes the public exit-code constants: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from `4` to `3` and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` in `CompatibilityResult` (`int RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 3; int FEATURE_DISABLED = 4;`). That is a behavioral/contract change for any external automation that interprets exit codes, and the diff does not show any compatibility shim or migration note beyond comments. Whether it definitively “breaks every external caller” isn’t provable from the diff, but the compatibility risk the finding describes is grounded in this renumbering.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The custom image is built with --features=rolling-updates unconditionally, which creates rolling-deploy skew in the upgrade test path this image exists for: the old-version image in an upgrade chain cannot contain this feature, so the very first rolling upgrade from any prior Keycloak version runs with old pods that lack the feature the new operator flow (per the docs' CAUTION) requires. Users attempting the first-ever rolling upgrade into this version hit the bootstrap gap: the feature flag cannot be enabled on the pre-upgrade pods, so the documented hard requirement ('otherwise the Operator will fail') makes the transition rolling-update path impossible or forces a Recreate upgrade for the initial hop — the docs never state this one-version bootstrap restriction.
